There are many different kinds of Perfect modals to express certainty or uncertainty.

Clauses Using -ing with Verbs of Perception
You can use these verbs to talk about perception: feel, hear, notice, observe, see, watch, and overhear.
You can use these verbs with either an object + -ing or object + bare infinitive. Depending on the structure you choose, the meanings will be slightly different.

For example:
I saw them playing soccer from my window. (-ing indicates that the action was in progress)
I saw him kick the ball. (bare infinitive indicates that the action is completed)

I was able to watch them building the new stadium from my window. (-ing suggests that I watched, but not from the start to the finish)
I watched him climb through the window and then I called security. (bare infinitive implies I watched the whole action from start to finish)

Recently James had noticed his friends becoming more and more worried about his love life. He admitted that he would have done more to go out and find someone, but he was quite content with the life he and Lacey had in his cozy little apartment.
“I watch you waste your time, and I'm worried,” his friend Steve complained. “Last week I sent you a link to that online dating site, and you completely ignored it.”
“I know I should have signed up,” James replied. “But Lacey and I had plans to take a quiet stroll in the forest."

“And then I gave you that girl's number,” Steve continued. “I overheard her saying that she thought you were cute, but you never even called.”
“Well I might have called,” James answered. “But Lacey and I decided to snuggle and watch Netflix instead. We really needed to unwind. We had a busy afternoon.”
“You can't have been all that busy,” Steve replied. “I saw you shopping at the farmers market with Lacey that afternoon!”

“Oh, right, it must have slipped my mind,” James responded. “That was a charming little market.”
“And what about the matchmaker who had an office right down the street?” Steve asked. “I gave you her address last week.”
“I could have gone,” James answered. “But Lacey had an appointment to get her nails done, and she must have been a little sore, because she also wanted me to rub her back for a while ... ”
“Lacey, Lacey, Lacey! If you aren't careful, you're going to end up a grumpy old bachelor,” Steve shouted in an exasperated tone. “You need to find someone new!”
“If I have Lacey, why do I need anyone else?” James asked.
“Because Lacey is your dog, not your girlfriend!” Steve replied, shaking his head.
